# CP/TNI cavity receiving for a processor beside a protected native bank
30 October 2026. Root construction candidate, independent review pending. This is not permission to condition on an unobserved successful event and pretend the noise is unchanged.

## 1. A precise extension of the already accepted cavity algebra
Let the finite bounded scheduled processor generator be

 K(t)=L_id(t)+K_B,raw(t)+sum_e M_e(t),

on processor S and retained B. The TOTAL generator has CP and trace-NONINCREASING propagators on every interval. Each M_e is HP, supported on at most q processor sites plus arbitrary B, with the same bounded per-processor-site incident diamond-norm sum. Individual M_e need not annihilate trace. Intended L_id gates are the usual CPTP generators on disjoint active processor blocks.

For selected processor blocks R define the same normalized partial-trace generator projection P_R and

 K^R=L_id+P_R(K-L_id)=P_R K+sum_(j in R)L_id,j.

The reduced short-step maps Tr_R exp(hK) E_R are CP/TNI, equal the identity at h=0, and have derivative Tr_R K E_R. Their repeated-product limit is CP/TNI. Hence each K^R and each convex cavity interpolation is CP/TNI, with complete norm at most1 between derivative insertions.

The remaining accepted proof is unchanged: a term NOT touching a differentiated processor block is killed by P_j-I whether or not that term is trace annihilating. Norms of the projections are still at most1. The same ordered-partition estimate, rooted recursion, Möbius cancellation and fault-location LINEAR-SPAN support therefore give

 ||sum_(F contains S0)E_F||_diamond
 <=[2*3^(q-1)g eta tau]^(|S0|/q).

E_empty is the ideal processor circuit tensored with a TNI bath map. Exact-target approximate-gate slots are received in the same way: fixed difference insertions multiply norms, while all intervening maps are CP/TNI contractions. Strength becomes product_(j in S0)(x+delta_j).

This is a statement for a whole CP/TNI generator, not arbitrary nonpositive conditional evolution. No positivity of an individual local M_e or signed fault map is used. Bounded finite-dimensional/domain assumptions remain as in the accepted core.

## Verdict

**PASS for the CP/TNI, not-necessarily-centered local-perturbation extension of the finite scheduled cavity theorem.** Its conditional native-killed application is sound with the explicit logical-factorization and common-source-domain requirements below. The accompanying TRACE_FACTOR_COMPLETION.md supplies a precise factor-two normalization result under those requirements.

This does not independently prove the native bank's logical factorization, its full-versus-killed boundary estimate, or a complete concurrent hybrid architecture. A processor-independent cut is necessary here but does not by itself imply native logical identity.

## 1. Positivity and contraction survive the TNI replacement

For any selected processor block R, the short-step map Tr_R exp(hK) E_R is CP/TNI, is the identity at h=0, and has derivative Tr_R K E_R. In the finite bounded model its repeated-product limit is a CP/TNI semigroup. Tensoring the identity on R and restoring the independent intended CPTP generators on R gives

 K^R=P_R K+sum_(j in R)L_id,j.

This is CP/TNI. Trace preservation of the intended gates is sufficient for the same identity as in the core proof, including nonunital gates. Convex combinations of these generators remain CP/TNI. A CP/TNI map has complete trace norm at most one, since its adjoint maps I to an operator between0 and I. Equality to one was never required in the Duhamel/partition estimate.

The derivative norm bound, support cutoff |A|<=q, ordered set-partition argument and rooted incidence recursion are therefore unchanged.

# Explicit positive auxiliary repair and factor-two error budget
30 October 2026. Completion of the TNI cavity receiving note. This is an algebraic receiving lemma with a common channel-domain premise, not a new native-memory proof.

Let F be the FULL decoded CPTP channel from L_in tensor A_in to L_out tensor A_out. L may contain both the native and processor logical registers and their intended joint logical operation U is CPTP. Let K be the decoded native-killed CP/TNI channel on that SAME input/output chart. Suppose

 ||F-K||_diamond<=epsilon,
 K=G+B,  ||B||_diamond<=b,
 G=U tensor A,

where A is a signed linear auxiliary map. The last identity is actual logical factorization of the good fault classes, not an inference from marginal channel fidelities. Then ||F-U tensor A||_diamond<=epsilon+b.

Choose any fixed normalized logical input state sigma and define

 A_+(X)=Tr_(L_out) F(sigma tensor X).

A_+ is an actual CPTP channel. Applying the same CPTP insertion/partial-trace maps to F-U tensor A gives

 ||A_+-A||_diamond<=epsilon+b,

because Tr U(sigma)=1. Since ||U||_diamond=1,

 ||F-U tensor A_+||_diamond<=2(epsilon+b).             (TF1)

This preserves arbitrary logical/reference inputs and performs no survival conditioning. A_+ need not be physically implemented: it is a legitimate comparison auxiliary channel extracted from the actual full process. It also avoids assuming the signed good auxiliary map is CP or TP.

The lemma remains valid after a declared source channel I_L tensor E_aux, with all norms on its common parameter/input space. For a fixed auxiliary preparation, A reduces to a signed scalar/output-state map and the same proof applies. It does NOT justify changing the auxiliary assignment with an unknown logical input, proving separate pointwise bounds on incompatible input domains, or applying an extraction product probe outside the source class on which epsilon is controlled.

A native theorem whose bound is only a weighted warm-state estimate must explicitly provide a common source/channel chart, uniform in the admitted logical and processor input and retained references, before TF1 is quoted as a diamond-channel guarantee. Otherwise retain its original state-restricted norm and do not silently promote it.
